name: Cardiac Anomalies in Heterotaxy Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of complex congenital heart defects including atrioventricular septal defects, transposition of great arteries, or single ventricle physiology
Abnormal arrangement of thoracoabdominal organs (situs ambiguous) demonstrated by imaging
Presence of asplenia or polysplenia detected clinically or radiologically
Bronchial tree morphology consistent with right or left isomerism on imaging
Anomalous systemic or pulmonary venous return identified by echocardiography or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complex congenital heart defects plus abnormal situs on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and imaging-based; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complex congenital heart defects (e.g., atrioventricular septal defect)
searchTerms: severe heart structural abnormalities at birth
abnormal organ positioning in chest and abdomen
disorganized arrangement of chest and belly organs
spleen abnormalities including no spleen or many spleens

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy

occasional.symptomName: Arrhythmias including atrial flutter or fibrillation
searchTerms: abnormal heartbeats like flutter or fibrillation

occasional.symptomName: Intestinal malrotation with or without volvulus
searchTerms: intestinal rotation problems with or without twisting

occasional.symptomName: Chronic hypoxemia due to cyanotic heart disease
searchTerms: low oxygen levels from blue heart disease
chronic low blood oxygen due to heart defect
low platelet count from spleen issues
reduced blood platelets due to spleen
weakened immune system from no spleen
immune deficiency due to absent spleen

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear may show Howell-Jolly bodies indicating asplenia
Thrombocytopenia or leukopenia in cases with splenic dysfunction
imaging: Echocardiography revealing complex congenital heart defects
Chest and abdominal CT or MRI showing abnormal organ arrangement and bronchial isomerism
Radionuclide spleen scan demonstrating absent or multiple splenic tissue
genetic: Mutations in genes such as ZIC3, CFC1, and NODAL associated with heterotaxy
Genetic heterogeneity with variable inheritance patterns
other: Clinical examination revealing cyanosis and heart murmurs
Increased susceptibility to infections due to splenic abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Complete mirror-image reversal of organ placement
Usually no complex congenital heart defects

redFlags: Severe cyanosis and hypoxemia in neonate
Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
references: Lin AE, et al. Heterotaxy: associated conditions and hospital-based prevalence in newborns. Am J Med Genet A. 2014.
Mahle WT, et al. Heterotaxy syndrome: clinical and genetic aspects. Pediatr Cardiol. 2016.
